source_refs.note: Sub-heading 'Network Interface Card (NIC)' of 1.4 as printed (PDF 9, printed 4).

blocks.text: A Network Interface Card allows a device to connect to a network (as shown in Figure 1.6). It can be wired or wireless. Each NIC has a unique address called MAC address. The NIC sends and receives data from the network. Without a NIC, a device cannot communicate on a network. NICs are built into most modern devices.

blocks.alt: A network interface card: a green circuit board with chips and a gold edge connector, fixed to a metal bracket; the socket on the bracket is labelled Ethernet Port.
blocks.caption: Figure 1.6: Network Interface Card (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 1.6).
